elements.element: Company may assign the Agreement to an affiliate without Contractor's consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly disapplies the consent requirement for an assignment by Company to an affiliate.

elements.element: Company may assign the Agreement to a successor in a merger without Contractor's consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment by Company to a successor in a merger without consent.

elements.element: Company may assign the Agreement to a successor in an acquisition without Contractor's consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment by Company to a successor in an acquisition without consent.

elements.element: Company may assign the Agreement to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets without Contractor's consent.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment by Company to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets without consent.

elements.element: Contractor may not assign the Agreement without Company's consent.
elements.evidence: The original mutual restriction remains operative and requires Company's express, prior written consent for any Contractor assignment.

elements.element: Company may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Contractor assignment.
elements.evidence: The unchanged consent provision states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld; the specific competitor prohibition governs competitor assignments.

elements.element: Contractor may never assign the Agreement to a competitor of Company.
elements.evidence: The proviso states categorically that Contractor shall not assign the Agreement to a competitor of Company.

elements.element: Contractor has no termination right triggered by Company's change of control.
elements.evidence: No operative language grants Contractor a termination right upon Company's change of control. The termination-payment paragraph only addresses consequences of termination under other sections and does not create such a right.

elements.element: Company may assign the Agreement to any successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Company's no-consent right is limited to successors in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets rather than successors without qualification.

elements.element: Company must provide written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: The proviso contains no written-notice requirement for a Company successor assignment.

elements.element: Contractor may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: The successor exception applies only to Company; Contractor remains subject to Company's prior written consent for successor assignments.

elements.element: Contractor must provide written notice when assigning the Agreement to a successor.
elements.evidence: No Contractor successor-assignment right or corresponding written-notice mechanism is provided.

elements.element: Contractor's consent is required for every Company assignment other than an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: Company may assign to an affiliate without consent even where that affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Contractor may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Company assignments.
elements.evidence: For Company assignments that remain subject to consent, the unchanged mutual provision states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Company's consent is required for every Contractor assignment other than an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The unchanged mutual restriction requires Company's express, prior written consent for all Contractor assignments, including non-successor assignments.

elements.element: Company may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Contractor assignments.
elements.evidence: Although the general consent sentence contains a reasonableness qualifier, the specific competitor prohibition categorically forecloses assignment to a class of non-successors even with consent, so the fallback consent standard does not govern all other Contractor assignments.

result.reason: The operative proviso reaches the complete preferred position by creating the requested Company affiliate and transaction-successor exceptions, preserving the reasonableness-qualified consent requirement for Contractor, and imposing an absolute competitor prohibition. No change-of-control termination right appears. The fallback is not satisfied because successor rights are not mutual, neither party has the required written-notice mechanism, and the Company affiliate and Contractor competitor provisions depart from the fallback's uniform consent regime. The amendment is substantively minimal, although drafting quality is reduced by placing the proviso after an intervening termination paragraph, using the somewhat awkward phrase “successor in an acquisition,” and leaving “competitor” undefined.
